description: For **46** years, South Africa legally organized racial segregation. **Nelson Mandela**, after **27** years in prison, helps the country emerge without civil war.

hero.hook: A system of total segregation, then an end to the crisis without civil war.

blocks.text: In **1948**, as the world began to condemn state racism, South Africa took the opposite path. For **46 years**, it legally organized total segregation: the . **[[apartheid]]**

This regime collapsed at the beginning of the **1990** years without falling into civil war. At the center of this shift: **Nelson Mandela**, lawyer who became leader of the resistance, released after **27 years** of captivity.

The  ("separation" in Afrikaans) was implemented by the National Party after May **1948**. Each citizen is classified: White, Black, Colored, Indian. This label decides on voting, work, place of life. **[[apartheid]]**

blocks.caption: Segregation signs: public space divided by law.

blocks.text: The , reserves supposed to be “national homes” for blacks, only cover **13%** of the territory. In reality, they serve to strip them of South African citizenship. Without a pass, no movement in white zones: prison awaits. **[[The bantustans]]**
For commercial reasons, the Japanese were officially classified as “Honorary Whites.” Racism knew how to bow to the markets.

The , the African National Congress, organizes the resist**[[ANC]]**e. Mandela, born in **1918**, first believed in non-violence. Then comes  (March **1960**): the police shoot at an unarmed crowd protesting against the passes. Results: **69** dead. **[[The Sharpeville massacre (March 1960)]]**

The ANC is banned. Mandela co-founded Umkhonto we Sizwe (“The Spear of the Nation”) to sabotage the regime apparatus. Arrested in **1962**, sentenced to life at the Rivonia trial (**1964**), he became the most famous political prisoner in the world on Robben Island.

In the years **1980**, sanctions, embargo and uprisings suffocated the regime. **Frederik Willem de Klerk**, white president who came to power in **1989**, understands that survival requires the end of apartheid.

**February 11, 1990**, Mandela released from prison. Four years of negotiations followed. In April **1994**, the first elections open to all: the ANC won and Mandela became president with **62.6%** of the votes, in a government of national unity.

In **1995**, Mandela puts on the green jersey of the Springboks, the national rugby team that has long been an Afrikaner symbol, during the World Cup: a gesture of reconciliation seen around the world.

With Archbishop **Desmond Tutu**, Mandela is banking on reconciliation. The  proposes amnesty in exchange for public confessions: a  to know the fate of the victims without blowing up the country. **[[The Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC)]]** **[[transitional justice]]**
Mandela left power in **1999** after just one term. Legal racism is dead. Economic inequalities remain South Africa’s great challenge.

blocks.text: The  (**1948-1994**) was a system of state racial segregation. Its fall, negotiated by Mandela and de Klerk, opened a multiracial democracy based on reconciliation. **[[apartheid]]**
